summary_en: Ajinomoto proposes selective capital reduction (SCR) of Ajinomoto (Malaysia) Berhad (50.38% owned) targeting 30,170,689 shares (non-parent holders) at 20.0 MYR/share (803 yen); total capital repayment 603.4M MYR (24.2B yen); completion ~6 months pending AMB board decision, shareholder approval, and court authorization; delisting from Bursa Malaysia main market upon completion.
title_en: Notice Regarding Proposal for Full Subsidiary Acquisition of Ajinomoto (Malaysia) Berhad through Selective Capital Reduction
translation_en_brief: On 22 June 2026, Ajinomoto Co. announced a proposal to its subsidiary Ajinomoto (Malaysia) Berhad (AMB) — a listed company on Bursa Malaysia's main market in which Ajinomoto holds 50.38% ownership — to execute a selective capital reduction (SCR) under Malaysia's Companies Act 2016. Under the SCR mechanism, non-parent shareholders would receive cash repayment at 20.0 Malaysian ringgit (approximately 803 yen) per share, totaling 603.4 million MYR (24.2 billion yen) across 30,170,689 shares. Upon completion, those shares would be cancelled, making AMB a wholly owned subsidiary and triggering delisting from Bursa Malaysia's main market. The stated rationale is to accelerate operational agility and strengthen global business coordination within the Ajinomoto group. AMB's board will evaluate the proposal and determine implementation. Completion is contingent on AMB board approval, extraordinary shareholder meeting authorization, and court sanction, a process typically requiring approximately 6 months in Malaysia. The transaction is expected to have negligible impact on Ajinomoto's consolidated financial statements for fiscal 2026.
